commentary: Sub-continent market pricing continued its healthy course offering mid and high 500/LDT for the right ships. Pakistan stayed on the leading position for another week, despite Bangladesh’s recovery on the market and the impressive high priced deals. In addition, India’s steel prices were declined last week, due to the Indian Rupee depreciation over the past weeks.

Firm prices continued to prevail in the ship recycling market, primarily owed to the lack of available tonnage, with the End Buyers giving rates of high 500/LDT. Pakistan remained a strong competitor in the market, but lost the lead to an incredible Bangladeshi market. India’s supply of specialist vessels was steady, along with some green vessels, however that was not able to move them from the last place of the market.

Sub-Continent market steel prices improved over the past week continuing its uplifting course. Bangladesh pricing improved further, with few sales over USD 600/LDT. Pakistan remained closed to its Bangladesh counter parts, in the race of the market pricing. India on the other hand had a rough past weeks due to declining local steel prices, but India’s market progressed forward last week and tried to compete with her counter parts.

Bangladeshi market continued its impressing course, despite the period of Eid holidays, in addition with Pakistani market which lost several well placed vessels. For Indian market is a very positive time, with the increasing rates of steel plate prices and Indian Rupee rates against US Dollar. Turkey remained closed for the entire working week due to the Eid celebration, so there were no offers or indications.

At the end of the EID holidays, the supply of tonnage was shortened. Bangladesh had a difficult time to secure vessels despite the fact of the outstanding numbers excess 600/LDT. Pakistan started to understand that they have to step up their game to compete with their counterparts. On the other hand, India regained ground on market pricing and tried to get as many vessels from their rivals as they could.

The demolition prices continued to rise, driven by scarcity of available tonnage. Despite the concerns and the lockdown restrictions from the surge of Covid-19, the upturn of the recycling markets seem will be continued in the rest of summer/monsoon months. Bangladesh maintained its uplifting course with prices above the barrier of USD 600/LTD. The same upward trend had been followed by Pakistani recyclers. Meanwhile, India’s prices had been subdued mainly by transport strike in Alang.
